cohort: 23,735 women consecutively delivering singleton, live-born term infants in a single tertiary obstetrics centre in the UK (2004-2008)
finding: Significant seasonal variation was found in gestational diabetes incidence, birth weight in affected pregnancies, and emergency Caesarean rates, with the highest average birth weight and greatest risk of emergency Caesarean delivery occurring in women delivering during the spring months.
mod_finding: Emergency Caesarean rates showed significant seasonal variation of up to 50%, which was closely temporally correlated with increased birth weights.
